payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: What color is the DVD?
node.criteria: complete if the DVD is white; partial if it has changed from black toward white but is not white; absent if it remains black with no requested change; unknown if evidence is insufficient.
node.binding: Target: the black DVD; reference: a white DVD.

node_traces.evidence: The DVD near the center-right is white in the edited image, whereas the DVD in the source appears dark; the requested color change is complete.
The DVD near the center-right is white in the edited image, whereas the corresponding DVD in the source is dark.
The DVD is white in the edited image, whereas the small disc in the source appears dark.
The DVD near the center is white in the edited image, whereas it appeared dark in the source.
The DVD-like disc is white in the edited image, whereas the corresponding object in the source appears dark.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s target binding is ambiguous and appears inconsistent with the images: the source shows a small square DVD case near the center, while the edited image shows two circular discs, one white near center-left and another white near center-right. The traces repeatedly call the center-right disc the DVD and report complete, but do not establish which edited object corresponds to the source DVD/case; the aggregate “yes” therefore conflicts with the reference “no” without identifying the visual failure. Tighten the binding to the source object using its location/appearance and require comparison with that same object in the edited image, rather than accepting any white disc as the target. Make the criterion explicitly distinguish complete, partial, absent, and unresolved based on visible evidence of the bound object’s color change; if correspondence cannot be established, return unknown rather than infer completion. Investigate the apparent extra disc/object and the source-to-edit correspondence, but do not treat repeated high-confidence traces as proof or force a “no” solely to match the reference. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
